relevant_negatives: no loss of taste or smell
history.social_history: No smoking, no vaping, occasional alcohol (1-2 drinks on weekends)

examination.findings: Throat slightly red, no pus or significant swelling; nasal congestion with clear discharge; mild tenderness around neck glands; chest clear, no wheezing or crackles; breathing comfortable.

assessment.clinical_impression: Consistent with a viral upper respiratory tract infection; no evidence of pneumonia or serious throat infection.

plan.follow_up: If not improving over the next week or cough persists beyond 3 weeks, return for reassessment.
safety_netting: seek urgent medical attention if develop difficulty breathing, chest pain, cough up blood, severe difficulty swallowing, persistent high fever, or sudden worsening
patient_instructions: take paracetamol if throat painful or feverish
take simple cough medicine at night if cough disrupts sleep
monitor symptoms and seek urgent care if severe symptoms arise
return if not improving after one week or cough lasts longer than three weeks
